subject: POC kickoff collision — propose split live hands-on + async prompt review
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@eldor.ai>, poc@eldor.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — proposed agenda, load-test windows, and prework

Hi Lara —

Looking forward to our POC kickoff. Quick note: we typically split the first working session into (1) a short prompt & routing review and (2) a hands-on routing + load test run so we can validate latency/cost and the KV cache behavior with your sample prompts.

Proposed 90-minute live slot (sample agenda):
- 0–15m: introductions + success criteria
- 15–35m: prompt walkthrough + expected routing patterns
- 35–75m: live hands-on: routing config + load tests (we’ll run a staged ramp)
- 75–90m: next steps and rollouts

Load-test options (pick one):
- Option A: steady 50 rps for 10 minutes (validate throughput)
- Option B: spike test 0→100 rps over 2 minutes (validate autoscale/fallback)

If the full hands-on doesn't work for your team in one block, we can do a 30–40m live routing + prompt review and then a separate 60m hands-on window (can be the same day or next).

Attachments: POC_Scoping_Sheet.xlsx (scope + roles), proposed-slot-poll.ics

Please confirm preferred slot(s) — we’ve penciled in the following tentative slots in PT:
- Wed Jun 23, 10:00–11:30
- Wed Jun 23, 15:00–16:30
- Thu Jun 24, 09:00–10:30

Also tell us which load-test option you prefer and who will be the primary contact for network/firewall access.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
[Attachment: POC_Scoping_Sheet.xlsx]

From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@eldor.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: poc@eldor.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — proposed agenda, load-test windows, and prework

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the thorough plan. Apologies — a last-minute company-wide all-hands collided with our Wed morning slot, so we won’t be able to make the 10:00 PT window. We still want the hands-on, but to make it lower friction for our engineers I’d prefer splitting into: (A) a focused 30–40m live prompt/routing review, and (B) a separate 60m hands-on load-test window (Ben and I can cover the prework asynchronously).

We’d like Option B (spike test) to see the autoscale behavior.

Available windows on our side (PT):
- Wed Jun 23, 15:00–16:00 — good for the short live review
- Thu Jun 24, 11:00–12:30 — okay for the hands-on load test

One more ask: we had a calendar-sync issue on our side last week that caused one of our engineers to miss a run; can you include a calendar invite + an .ics we can import? Also, could you drop an async prompt review doc so Ben can review prior to the hands-on?

Thanks,
Lara
Lara Chen
Head of Data Platforms, Eldor Analytics
lara.chen@eldor.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — proposed agenda, load-test windows, and prework

Thanks — splitting makes total sense. We’ll do exactly that:

Plan:
- Wed Jun 23, 15:00–15:40 PT: live prompt + routing review (30–40m)
- Thu Jun 24, 11:00–12:00 PT: hands-on spike load test (60m)

We’ll run spike Option B (0→100 rps). For the hands-on I’ll have Marissa run the staged ramp and Ben will monitor token costs and fallback rates.

Prework we’ll share: async-prompt-review.md — contains prompt variants, expected routing maps, and example KV-cache warmup commands. I’ve attached it here and added the slot .ics. You’ll see a quick checklist for network ports (to avoid firewall pauses during the spike).

Marissa — can you confirm runbook readiness and whether we need to provision a dedicated burst pool for the 100 rps spike?

On Thu I’ll keep an eye on traces and telemetry so we can iterate in real time.

Cheers,
Priyom
